newsitem.title: USA: ECC recommends holders vote against Taglich.
newsitem.headline: ECC recommends holders vote against Taglich.

text.p: ECC International Corp said on Wednesday that proposals by shareholder Michael Taglich, who started a proxy fight with ECC, were not in the company's best interests.
It urged shareholders to vote against the proposals, which included a recommendation to hire an investment bank to sell ECC or its businesses, and changes to ECC by-laws.

Earlier on Wednesday, Taglich, who owned 1,000 ECC shares said he started a proxy contest and proposed bylaw changes to allow shareholders owning 10 percent or more of the company's shares to call a special meeting at any time.
Taglich also said the company's recent bylaw changes were insincere because they could be changed by the board at any time and did not require shareholder approval.
ECC had proposed allowing holders of 30 percent of the common stock to call special meetings. Taglich said this threshold was unreasonable.
ECC, answering to criticism it had been unresponsive to Taglich's proposals, said it had held several discussions with Taglich about them but Taglich was uncompromising.

It said that according to its research, about 200 S&P 500 companies had bylaws requiring shareholders hold between 25 percent and 100 percent of the shares outstanding in order to call special meetings.
With respect to Taglich's proposal that ECC pursue a sale of the company, ECC reiterated that uncertainty over future control of the company would jeopardize potential contracts.
